key_insight: Sleep-related CSF pulse trains strongly reorganize third-ventricle flow, creating preferential caudal/rostral streaming and much less recirculation than awake forcing.
engineering_relevance: The result suggests that time-varying physiologic forcing can dramatically alter intraventricular transport efficiency, which matters for models of CSF exchange, clearance, and neurofluidic device design.
method: Transient CFD simulations in the human third ventricle
Comparison of awake versus sleep-related pressure-pulse forcing
Evaluation of residual streaming and recirculation patterns
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that streaming flux relative to stroke volume increased from about 0.540% in the awake case to 28.4% during sleep-related forcing.
watch_item: The findings come from CFD in the third ventricle, so physiological variability, boundary-condition assumptions, and patient-to-patient anatomy may limit direct generalization.
paper_title: Sleep-related forcing of cerebrospinal fluid streaming transport through the third ventricle
